chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl bin Ziyad and Ahmad bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So whoever performs Hajj and Umrah together, then whatever offering is easy to obtain,' he (peace be upon him) said: 'A sheep.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum sacrificial animal required for Qiran Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the minimum sacrificial obligation for Qiran pilgrims, establishing a sheep as the sufficient 'easy-to-obtain' offering. It reflects the Shia juristic consensus on the literal interpretation of the Quranic phrase 'what is easy,' providing a practical baseline for ritual compliance that balances religious duty with economic accessibility.
